heading: New RGV capital projects group tackles infrastructure, workforce challenges

paragraphs.text: The Valley has long sat at the end of the line electrically.

ERCOT has treated the Lower Rio Grande Valley as a constrained pocket for years, served by long distance 345 kilovolt circuits running down from the north, with limited conventional generation inside the region and none of it planned.

In the study that supported the current round of upgrades, the grid operator projected summer peak demand in the Valley reaching 3,200 megawatts and found potential reliability criteria violations at or above that level even with no equipment outages.
